chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: Straightening out the dates with the 369th
summary: Briggs admits confusing his dates and clarifies he stayed with the 369th band until early 1919, after the war ended.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, tell me about the band. The group was all reading band, I mean it wasn't a jazz band?
You're talking about our band or the 369th?
Well, which band were you -- you left right away to go off with Will Marion Cook?
No, I didn't leave right away. I say that I continued, I continued with the band.
I think there's a real mistake about dates. I think that I really messed up my dates. It was so long ago. I mean one year or two -- I was seventeen, eighteen, when I came up why I was eighteen.
I was eighteen and we came over in '19. I was eighteen.
Okay, so in other words, you continued with the 369th?
Yes, I continued -- the 369th, you see, we -- I was with the 369th. That was in 1918. No, the beginning of 1919. The war had just finished.
